body:
**Agent review** of the whole pull request, at `3ec7a13`: all 23 files reviewed.

4 finding(s): 4 to consider; 4 on their lines. Reply in a comment's thread to answer it.

### Summary

**Batch 1 of 2.** Part 1 turns the camera off and on mid-take without ending the webcam file. The bubble window is parked instead of destroyed, and the encoder reads from a relay track, so the file keeps running and gaps are recorded. Each step checks the others' state consistently: main's `takeRecordsWebcam` and the engine's `webcamLive`/relay checks. Cleanup is done in order: `recordingStop` reaches main only after `recordingFinalize`, so `placedBounds` still reads the parked bubble's position. Gap segments are seeded and merged correctly. No blockers. One consider-level bug: if the camera can't be reopened, the face falls back to the same re-shown window, which may not be captured. That relies on main's best-effort unprotect, while the parked path creates a new window. There is also a misleading comment about the queue, and a test name that claims coverage of the hub reset it doesn't test. mediabunny isn't installed in this checkout, so I couldn't confirm that its `sizeChangeBehavior` and `frameRate` options exist.

**Batch 2 of 2.** Part 2 has one minor finding and nothing that blocks the merge.

- **Shared code:** `webcam-track.ts` has only relative imports, so nothing new reaches the preload bundle. The new gap sanitizer handles bad input from the renderer: it drops malformed, empty and backwards gaps, clamps starts before 0, sorts, merges overlaps and caps the list at 1000.
- **Tests:** they match how the gap log, the relay and the seeding code actually behave.
- **Docs:** the ADR 0032 decision 6 and the spec item 7 agree with the engine and store behaviour shown in the tests. That covers the fallback without a relay, refusing "off" before the take begins, trailing gaps, and a camera that can't be reopened.
- **Finding (consider):** one relay test comment claims a late frame from a cut camera is closed, but that code path never runs in the test and no assertion checks it.

> [!IMPORTANT] > One concrete regression: seeded gap segments get random ids, so Share's export reuse never matches for a take that has a camera-off gap. Everything else checks out. **Reviewed changes** Reviewed the full PR (4 commits): keeping one webcam file through a camera turned off and on mid-take, from the hub's park-vs-destroy down to editor seeding. - **Park instead of destroy (main)** — During a take with a live webcam file, camera off now hides and keeps the protected bubble window, and camera on shows the same native window again. A webcam file that ended while the bubble was parked falls back to a new unprotected window. Parked windows are released at stop, finalize, abort and reset. The other hub paths (`raise`, `anchorTo`, `applySize`, restore after a screenshot) never re-show a parked window. - **Bubble preview follows the toggle** — `useCameraOn` lets the hidden bubble release its camera, so the in-use light goes off. - **Relay track in the recorder engine** — The encoder reads a `MediaStreamTrackGenerator` that the current camera feeds. I checked this against mediabunny 1.61.4's `MediaStreamVideoTrackSource._start`: with an explicit `frameRate`, output frames come from a 4 ms `tick` that repeats `_lastVideoFrame` at `first + count/rate`. So the file holds its last frame through a gap, and the new camera's own timestamps don't matter. The old code was already constant frame rate, because the rate came from the track's settings. - **Gap log in the store** — A gap opens on the toggle and closes when the first frame is back or the file ends. A gap still open at the stop closes at `durationMs`. A failed reopen sets the existing "camera wasn't available" notice. I traced supersession (off → on → off while the camera is opening) through the engine's `cameraRequest` and the store's queue, and it behaves correctly. - **Sidecar `webcam.gaps`** — Sanitized: malformed gaps are dropped, starts are clamped to 0, gaps are sorted and merged, and at most 1000 are kept. - **Editor seeding** — Each gap becomes a hidden webcam segment. Gaps shorter than `WEBCAM_MIN_SEGMENT_SECONDS` are stretched to it, and overlapping ones are merged.   ｜ [Fix all ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/niway-dev/kaipu-record/463?action=fix&review_id=5720263597) ｜ [Fix 👍s ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/niway-dev/kaipu-record/463?action=fix-approved&review_id=5720263597) ｜ [View workflow run](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/actions/runs/41153059096/job/124393741539) ｜ Using `claude-opus-5-5` ｜ [𝕏](https://x.com/pullfrogai)

> [!IMPORTANT] > One supersession gap is left in the store: a queued turn-on can open the camera after the user has already turned it off again. Everything else in the new commits checks out, and the random-id finding from the last review is fixed. **Reviewed changes** Reviewed the 7 commits pushed since the last Pullfrog review (`3ec7a13`): fallbacks for a webcam file that ends or stalls, supersession of the camera toggle, deterministic seeding, and docs. - **Bubble window replaced when the webcam file ends mid-take**: `bubbleRejoinsCapture` destroys a protected bubble that is on screen and recreates it unprotected at the same corner, because a running capture is known to record a new window. This also fixes the reopen-failure path from the earlier agent review: at turn-on the window is shown protected, so it gets replaced once the reopen fails. If a screenshot has the bubble hidden, the replacement waits for `restoreCameraBubbleAfterCapture`. - **Relay reports a lost camera**: `feed(camera, onLost)` reports a read error, write error or end that comes after the first frame, and does not report `cut`, a new `feed` or `stop`. The engine ends the file in that case, so it never holds a frame with no gap to hide it. - **First-frame and reopen deadlines**: the take's own camera now has 3 s after `webcam.output.start()` to deliver a frame. Turning the camera on uses one `deadlineIn` for both opening it and getting its first frame. - **Only the newest turn-on closes a gap**: `webcamOnRequest` stops a superseded on from closing the gap early. - **Deterministic gap ids, duration-aware `reconcileWebcam`**: ids derive from the segment start, so Share's `wholeFingerprint` is stable (covered by a test). Saved sessions reseeded through `reconcileWebcam` now keep trailing gaps inside the recording. - **Bubble preview waits for the toggle**: `useCameraOn` starts off until main answers, so a window parked before ready never lights the camera.   ｜ [Fix all ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/niway-dev/kaipu-record/463?action=fix&review_id=5720337044) ｜ [Fix 👍s ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/niway-dev/kaipu-record/463?action=fix-approved&review_id=5720337044) ｜ [View workflow run](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/actions/runs/41154789953/job/124399098677) ｜ Using `claude-opus-5-5` ｜ [𝕏](https://x.com/pullfrogai)
